If you really like a particular company, you can send a **speculative application**. Sometimes this leads to a chance even though no place was advertised.

Many apprenticeship places are given out through **contacts** before they are advertised publicly. That is why it is worth telling your parents, relatives, neighbours and acquaintances what you are looking for. Coaches at your sports club or teachers sometimes know a company too. This **network** can give valuable tips.

If you write lots of applications, you can quickly lose track. An **application list** shows when you applied where and how things stand. In it you note the date, the company, the contact person and the answer. If there is no answer after about **two weeks**, you may politely **follow up** by phone or email. This shows interest and commitment.

If it has worked out, an **apprenticeship contract** is signed. If the apprentice is not yet of age, the parents or the **legal guardian** also sign. After that the canton approves the contract. Once you have accepted a place, you **politely withdraw** all your other open applications. This way those companies can give the place to other young people.

Rejections are part of looking for an apprenticeship place and are normal. The important thing is to learn from them and keep going. The canton's **careers advice service** helps with the search and with improving your application. If you still have no apprenticeship place in the summer, you can attend a **bridging programme**, for example a tenth school year, and keep applying.

gewusst: In Switzerland most apprenticeships begin in August.
Many companies give out their apprenticeship places almost a year before the apprenticeship starts.

teile.einleitung: Bricklayers build walls on the building site from bricks and concrete. Without them there would be no houses, schools or bridges.
wichtigste: A bricklayer builds walls from stones and concrete.
Stones are joined with mortar so that the wall holds.
Concrete consists of cement, sand, gravel and water.
For straight walls the bricklayer needs a spirit level, a line and a plumb bob.
In Switzerland the apprenticeship as a bricklayer EFZ lasts three years.
The work usually takes place outdoors, in all weathers.

abschnitte.text: A **bricklayer** places stones on top of each other and so builds walls. He often uses **bricks** made of fired clay or **sand-lime bricks**. With the **trowel** he spreads **mortar** between the stones, a mixture of sand, binder and water. When the mortar hardens, the stones hold firmly together. The stones are laid staggered so that the wall is stable.

Many parts of a house are made of **concrete**, for example foundations, ceilings and cellar walls. Concrete consists of **cement**, sand, gravel and water. It is poured as a liquid into a mould, the **formwork**. Inside there are steel bars, the **reinforcement**. They make the concrete much stronger. After a few days the concrete is hard and the formwork can be removed.

A wall must stand **straight** and **vertical**. For this the bricklayer uses the **spirit level**, which shows whether something is horizontal or vertical. With a stretched **line** he keeps to the right line. The **plumb bob**, a weight on a string, points exactly downwards. He also reads **building plans** and measures where doors and windows will go.

In Switzerland the apprenticeship is called **bricklayer EFZ** and lasts three years. For a shorter training course there is the **construction assistant EBA**. Bricklayers usually work **outdoors**, in the heat in summer and in the cold in winter. They need strength, team spirit and a love of working with their hands. A helmet and safety boots are compulsory on the building site.

gewusst: The ancient Romans already knew a kind of concrete. The Pantheon in Rome has a huge dome made of Roman concrete that is almost 2000 years old.
A brick is just the right size to hold in one hand, so the bricklayer can use the trowel with the other hand.

teile.einleitung: Holidays are paid days off that all employees in Switzerland have a right to. Apprentices and all young people up to their 20th birthday get a particularly large number of holidays. They are entitled to at least five weeks a year.
wichtigste: All employees in Switzerland have a right to paid holidays.
Adults get at least four weeks of holiday a year.
Young people up to their 20th birthday get at least five weeks.
This also applies to apprentices.
Holidays may not be paid out as money while the employment lasts.
At least two weeks of holiday should be taken in one block.
The rules are set out in the Code of Obligations.

abschnitte.text: Holidays are days when you do not have to work but still receive your **wages**. They are there for rest, so that you stay healthy and able to work well. The right to holidays is set out in the **Code of Obligations** (OR). A company may not agree to fewer holidays than the minimum.

Adult employees get at least four weeks of holiday a year. Young people up to the end of their 20th year get at least **five weeks**. Many companies and collective labour agreements voluntarily give more. The exact number is written in the apprenticeship contract.

Apprentices no longer have school holidays as before, but holidays like other employees. As a rule they should take their holidays when there are no lessons at the **vocational school**. Exactly when is agreed with the training company. The company takes their wishes into account, but has a say in the final decision.

At least two weeks of holiday must be granted **in one block**. During your holidays you may not work for money at another company if this gets in the way of your rest. If you fall ill during your holidays, the days of illness with a doctor's certificate usually do not count as holiday. Holidays may not simply be paid out while you are employed.

It is worth discussing your holiday wishes with the company early. You should note down how many **days of holiday** you have already taken. If anything is unclear, the cantonal vocational training offices or trade unions can help. Public holidays such as Christmas or 1 August do not count as days of holiday.

begriffe.erklaerung: An important Swiss law which, among other things, governs employment contracts.
People who are employed and receive wages.
A contract between employers and trade unions for a whole industry.
The number of days of holiday that you are entitled to.

gewusst: Young people get more holidays than many adults because they are still developing.
People with a part-time job also have a right to holidays, simply in proportion.

teile.einleitung: People who work also need rest. That is why the Code of Obligations (OR) sets out how many holidays employees in Switzerland must get at least and how they are taken.
wichtigste: Adults get at least four weeks of holiday per year of service.
Up to the end of their 20th year it is at least five weeks.
At least two weeks of holiday must be taken in one block.
The employer decides when, but takes the employee's wishes into account.
Holidays may not be paid out as money while the employment lasts.
With an hourly wage and four weeks of holiday, the holiday supplement is about 8.33 per cent.

abschnitte.text: Under **Art. 329a OR**, adults are entitled to at least **four weeks** of holiday per year of service. Anyone who is not yet 20 gets at least **five weeks**. Apprentices benefit from this above all. Employment contracts or **collective labour agreements** may provide for more holidays, but never fewer.

abschnitte.titel: When and for how long in one go
abschnitte.text: The **employer** decides when the holidays are taken. However, the employer must take the employees' wishes into account as far as the business allows. According to **Art. 329c OR**, at least two weeks of holiday must be taken in one block. Only then is real rest possible.

Holidays should really be taken. That is why **Art. 329d OR** forbids replacing them with money while the employment lasts. One exception is the **holiday supplement** for irregular hourly wages. With four weeks of holiday you work 48 of the 52 weeks, so the supplement is 4 divided by 48, which is about **8.33 per cent**.

If you are absent through no fault of your own, for example because of illness, you do not simply lose holidays. A reduction is only allowed once the absence lasts more than a month in total. For the second and every further full month, holidays may be reduced by **one twelfth**.

Young people up to the end of their 30th year can take up to one week of **youth leave** every year. It is meant for leading or supervising roles in youth work outside school, for example running a camp. The employer does not have to pay wages for this week.

gewusst: With five weeks of holiday, the holiday supplement for an hourly wage is about 10.64 per cent.
Youth leave is set out in Art. 329e OR and is important for many camp leaders.

teile.einleitung: Teachers teach children and young people new things. They explain reading, writing, maths and much more and help every child to make progress in learning.
wichtigste: A teacher teaches children new things at school.
She prepares lessons, teaches and marks work.
In Switzerland teachers are trained at universities of teacher education.
There are teachers for kindergarten, primary school, lower secondary school and other schools.
Teachers work closely with parents and other professionals.
In German-speaking Switzerland the Lehrplan 21 curriculum applies.

abschnitte.text: A **teacher** explains new things in a way that children understand. She sets tasks, answers questions and helps when someone is stuck. Besides teaching, she has a lot to do: she **prepares lessons**, looks for materials, **marks** tests and writes assessments. She also makes sure that everyone in the class feels comfortable.

Teachers work at different **levels**. In **kindergarten** the youngest children learn through play. In **primary school**, reading, writing and maths are added. In **lower secondary school**, teachers often teach only a few subjects. Later there are teachers at Gymnasiums and vocational schools. **Special needs teachers** are also part of the team; they support children who need extra help.

In Switzerland you learn the job at a **university of teacher education**, PH for short. For kindergarten and primary school, the bachelor's degree takes three years. For lower secondary school you need a **master's degree**. During your studies you already teach school classes yourself on placements. This way you learn theory and practice together.

A teacher does not work alone. She talks to the **parents**, for example at parents' meetings. She plans with other teachers and works with the head teacher, the school social workers or the school psychology service. What is learned at school is set out in German-speaking Switzerland in the **Lehrplan 21** curriculum.

gewusst: Johann Heinrich Pestalozzi from Zurich is seen as one of the best-known educators in the world. He wanted to develop the head, heart and hand.
During the eleven years of compulsory schooling in Switzerland, a child spends many thousands of hours in lessons.

teile.einleitung: A collective labour agreement, GAV for short, sets the working conditions for many employees at once. It is negotiated between trade unions and the employers' side and is an important part of the Swiss social partnership.
wichtigste: A GAV is concluded between employees' associations and employers or their associations.
It must be concluded in writing.
A GAV declared generally binding applies to all companies in an industry.
While it is in force, the peace obligation applies.
An individual contract may only differ from the GAV in favour of the employees.
The Peace Agreement of 1937 is seen as the foundation stone of the social partnership.

abschnitte.text: Under **Art. 356 OR**, **employees' associations**, that is trade unions, conclude a GAV with employers or **employers' associations**. It sets, for example, minimum wages, working hours, holidays or extra pay. According to **Art. 356c OR** it must be concluded in writing. This also applies to joining and terminating it.

Normally a GAV only applies to the members of the associations. With a **declaration of general applicability**, it is extended to all employers and employees in an industry, including non-members. If the GAV covers several cantons, the **Federal Council** decides; otherwise the canton does.

Under **Art. 357a OR**, the parties commit themselves to keeping **industrial peace** on the questions that are settled. Strikes and lockouts on these points are ruled out while the agreement is in force. On 19 July 1937, employers and trade unions in the metal and engineering industry concluded the **Peace Agreement**. They wanted to settle conflicts through negotiation rather than strikes.

Each person also has their own **individual employment contract**. If it differs from the GAV to the disadvantage of the employee, that agreement is void and the rule of the GAV applies. Differences in favour of the employee are allowed. This is called the **favourability principle**.

In the main construction industry, the **National Framework Agreement**, LMV for short, applies. It sets wages, working hours and other conditions. The LMV has been declared generally binding and is negotiated between the industry's employers' association and the trade unions.

gewusst: Many GAVs only apply for a few years and are then negotiated again.
Apprentices can also benefit from a GAV, for example through extra holidays.

teile.einleitung: Forestry workers work outdoors in the forest. They fell trees with a chainsaw, plant young trees and look after paths and protection forests.
wichtigste: Forestry workers almost always work outdoors in the forest, in all weathers.
They fell trees with a chainsaw and prepare the timber.
They plant young trees and look after the young forest.
The apprenticeship as a forestry worker EFZ lasts three years.
Safety is very important, so they wear a helmet and cut-resistant clothing.

abschnitte.text: One important task is **felling trees**. With the **chainsaw**, forestry workers first saw a notch into the trunk and then make the felling cut. This makes the tree fall in the planned direction. After that they remove the branches from the trunk and cut it into pieces. The wood is used for building, furniture or heating.

Forestry workers **plant young trees** and protect them from deer, which like to eat the buds. They remove shrubs that take the light away from the young trees. They keep **forest paths** in good repair and build fences or small barriers. This keeps the forest healthy.

In the mountains the forest protects villages and roads from **avalanches**, **rockfall** and landslides. This forest is called **protection forest**. Forestry workers make sure that it stays stable and that young trees keep growing back.

The apprenticeship as a **forestry worker EFZ** lasts three years. Because the work can be dangerous, apprentices learn a lot about safety. They wear a **helmet** with ear protection and a face guard as well as **cut-resistant trousers**. After the apprenticeship you can train further to become a forester.

gewusst: About a third of Switzerland's area is covered with forest.
Clear-cutting, which means felling all the trees on a large area, is forbidden in Switzerland.

teile.einleitung: The payslip shows how much you earn and what is deducted from it. If you can read it, you understand why less arrives in your account than is written in your employment contract.
wichtigste: The gross wage is the agreed wage before deductions.
After the social insurance contributions are deducted, what remains is the net wage, which is paid out.
According to Art. 323 OR, unless otherwise agreed, wages are paid at the end of the month.
A 13th month's salary is not required by law, only if it has been agreed.
For your tax return you receive a salary certificate every year.
Foreign employees without a C settlement permit usually pay withholding tax.
Since 2025, under federal law, the child allowance has been at least 215 francs a month.

abschnitte.text: Right at the top of the **payslip** is the **gross wage**. With an hourly wage you multiply the hours by the hourly rate: 160 hours at 28.50 francs gives 4560 francs. Then come the **deductions**. What is left is the **net wage**. Under **Art. 323 OR**, unless otherwise agreed, wages must be paid at the end of the month, and the employer provides a written statement.

Contributions to **social insurance** are deducted from the gross wage. The most important are the **AVS** (old-age and survivors' insurance), the **IV** (disability insurance) and the **EO** (income compensation scheme), which together came to 5.3 per cent for employees in 2025. On top of this there is **unemployment insurance**, above a certain wage the **pension fund**, and often insurance for accidents in your free time. For the AVS and unemployment insurance, the employer pays the same amount again.

Many employees receive a **13th month's salary**. However, the OR does not require it. It only applies if it has been agreed in the employment contract, in a **collective labour agreement** or through long-standing practice. If an annual salary is paid in 13 parts, you divide by 13: with 71,500 francs that is exactly 5500 francs a month.

Something can also be added on the payslip. Parents receive **family allowances**. Since 1 January 2025, the **child allowance** under federal law has been at least 215 francs per child per month, and this amount also applies in 2026. For children aged 16 and over who are in training there is the higher **training allowance**. The cantons may pay more.

Once a year, employees receive the **salary certificate**. It summarises all wage payments and deductions and is attached to the **tax return**. For foreign employees without a **C settlement permit**, the employer usually deducts the tax directly from the wages and pays it to the canton. This is called **withholding tax**.

gewusst: Employees pay AVS contributions from 1 January after their 17th birthday.
You should keep your payslips, because they help with questions about insurance and taxes.

teile.einleitung: An apprenticeship contract is a written contract between the apprentice and the training company. It contains everything important about the apprenticeship, for example its length, the wages and the holidays. The canton must approve the contract for it to be valid.
wichtigste: The apprenticeship contract is concluded between the apprentice and the training company.
It must be in writing.
For those under 18, the parents also sign.
The cantonal vocational training office approves the contract.
It sets out the length of the apprenticeship, wages, working hours, holidays and probationary period.
There is a probationary period at the start of the apprenticeship.

abschnitte.text: The **apprenticeship contract** is a special employment contract for the apprenticeship. It sets out the rights and duties of the apprentice and the company. It must be concluded in writing. If the apprentice is not yet 18, the parents also sign.

The training company sends the contract to the cantonal **vocational training office**. The office checks whether everything is in line with the law and approves it. The canton then registers the apprentice with the vocational school. It also **supervises** the apprenticeship and helps when there are problems.

The contract states the job, the start and the length of the apprenticeship. It also includes the wages for each year, the **working hours** and the number of weeks of holiday. The probationary period and insurance are also covered. There is a standard form for these contracts throughout Switzerland.

Every apprenticeship begins with a **probationary period** of one to three months. During this time both sides can check whether they suit each other. During the probationary period the contract can be terminated with seven days' notice. With the canton's consent it can be extended to a maximum of six months.

After the probationary period you cannot simply terminate an apprenticeship contract. It can only be ended by mutual agreement or for serious reasons. The canton must then be informed. If there is a dispute, the **apprenticeship supervisors** mediate between the apprentice and the company.

begriffe.erklaerung: A binding agreement between two or more people.
The first period of the apprenticeship, during which it is easier to part ways.
An office of the canton that oversees apprenticeships and helps with problems.
The firm where apprentices learn their job.

gewusst: If an apprenticeship contract is ended, the canton often helps to find a new apprenticeship place.
In Switzerland tens of thousands of new apprenticeship contracts are signed every year.

teile.einleitung: Kita is short for Kindertagesstätte, a day nursery. Small children are looked after there during the day while their parents work or are in training.
wichtigste: Kita is short for Kindertagesstätte, a day nursery.
The Kita mainly looks after children before they start kindergarten.
The children play, eat, rest and learn a lot.
Trained childcare workers look after the children.
In Switzerland the cantons or municipalities license and supervise the Kitas.

abschnitte.text: A **Kita** is a place where small children are **looked after** during the day. Many children start there as babies and stay until they go to **kindergarten**. Some are there every day, others only on a few days a week. The parents bring them in the morning and pick them up again in the evening.

At the Kita there is a fixed **daily routine**. The children play indoors and outdoors, sing, do crafts and listen to stories. Together they have their mid-morning snack, lunch and afternoon snack. After lunch the little ones often have an **afternoon nap**. Fixed routines give the children a sense of security.

Children learn a great deal at the Kita, mostly while **playing**. They learn to share with other children and to sort out arguments. They practise new words and explore their surroundings. Children who speak another language at home often already learn the **local language** at the Kita.

At the Kita, **childcare workers** and apprentices work. The manager often has higher training, for example as an **early childhood educator HF**. For a Kita to be allowed to open, it needs a **licence**. Depending on the canton, the canton or the municipality grants and checks this licence.

gewusst: Since 2003 the Confederation has supported the creation of new childcare places with a funding programme.
Many municipalities in Switzerland contribute to Kita costs so that more families can afford a place.

teile.einleitung: Train drivers drive trains. At the front, in the driver's cab, they make sure that passengers and goods reach their destination safely and on time.
wichtigste: The train driver sits in the driver's cab and drives the train.
He pays attention to signals, the timetable and the speed.
Technical safety systems stop the train if something is wrong.
Train drivers drive passenger trains or goods trains.
In Switzerland the railway is very important, and the trains are known for their punctuality.
The training is usually done as an adult after a first qualification.

abschnitte.text: The **driver's cab** is the train driver's workplace right at the front of the train. There are levers for accelerating and braking, screens and a radio. The train driver pays attention to **signals** beside the track or on the screen, keeps to the permitted **speed** and follows the **timetable**. At every station the train has to stop at exactly the right spot.

A train is very heavy and has a long **braking distance**. That is why technical systems help. The **train protection system** brakes the train automatically if it would pass a red signal or is going too fast. A **vigilance device** checks whether the driver is awake and paying attention. If he does not react, the train stops by itself.

Some train drivers drive **passenger trains**, from suburban trains to long-distance trains. Others drive **goods trains** carrying containers, cars or gravel. Because trains run early in the morning and late in the evening, train drivers often work **shifts**, including at weekends. Before setting off, they check the vehicle, for example the brakes.

Switzerland has a dense **railway network**, and people here travel by train a great deal. The largest railway company is the **SBB**, and there are many other railways such as the BLS or the Rhaetian Railway. Anyone who wants to become a train driver usually first completes an apprenticeship or other training and then special **training** with a railway company, with an examination set by the Confederation.

gewusst: At about 57 kilometres, the Gotthard Base Tunnel is the longest railway tunnel in the world. It opened in 2016.
A goods train can need more than a kilometre of braking distance before it comes to a stop.

teile.einleitung: In the past people spoke of the Kleinkinderzieher, or nursery nurse. Today the job in Switzerland is called childcare worker (Fachfrau or Fachmann Betreuung). These professionals look after small children in the Kita.
wichtigste: Nursery nurse (Kleinkinderzieher) is an older name.
Today the job is called childcare worker (Fachfrau or Fachmann Betreuung), FaBe for short.
The apprenticeship lasts three years and ends with the EFZ.
Childcare workers work, for example, in a Kita.
They play, sing, eat and do crafts with the children.

abschnitte.text: At the **Kita**, childcare workers look after small children. They **play**, sing, eat and do crafts with them. They comfort a child who is sad and help with getting dressed or washing hands. They watch how each child is developing and tell the parents about it.

The work is carefully planned. Childcare workers think up **activities** that suit the children's age. They arrange the rooms so that the children can play safely and discover a lot. They pay attention to healthy food, rest times and **safety**. Working together as a team is also important.

The apprenticeship as a **childcare worker EFZ** lasts three years. You choose a **specialism**, for example **children**, older people or people with disabilities. There is also a general training course that combines several areas. Lessons take place at vocational school.

After the apprenticeship you can train further, for example as an **early childhood educator HF** at a college of higher education. With this you can, for example, lead a group or a whole Kita. Patience, a love of children and a sense of responsibility are important for the job.

gewusst: Men also work in this job, but there are still only a few of them.
The abbreviation FaBe is widely used in Switzerland for this job.

teile.einleitung: The fire brigade comes when there is a fire. But it also helps with accidents, floods, storm damage and many other emergencies.
wichtigste: The fire brigade puts out fires and rescues people and animals.
It helps with road accidents, floods and storm damage.
In Switzerland you can reach the fire brigade on the emergency number 118.
Most fire brigades in Switzerland are volunteer (militia) fire brigades.
Large cities also have a professional fire brigade.

abschnitte.text: You can remember the fire brigade's tasks with four words: **rescue**, **extinguish**, **recover** and **protect**. First, people and animals are brought to safety. Then the fire is put out. After that the fire brigade clears up and protects the surroundings from further damage.

Many call-outs have nothing to do with fire at all. During **floods** the fire brigade pumps out cellars and builds barriers out of sandbags. After a **storm** it clears away fallen trees. At road accidents it frees trapped people and soaks up spilled oil.

In Switzerland most firefighters are **militia firefighters**. They have another job and turn out when the alarm goes. They train regularly in their municipality. Large cities such as Zurich, Basel, Bern or Geneva also have a **professional fire brigade** that is ready round the clock.

People who want to work for a professional fire brigade have usually completed an apprenticeship first, for example in a craft trade. After that comes training as a **professional firefighter**. Good fitness, team spirit and a cool head are important.

gewusst: In many Swiss municipalities there is a duty to serve in the fire brigade. People who do not serve often pay a substitute tax.
Many fire brigades have a youth fire brigade, where children and teenagers can already take part.

teile.einleitung: Data protection means that personal information about people is protected and may not simply be collected, passed on or misused. In Switzerland the Data Protection Act regulates how companies and authorities must handle personal data. Data protection helps to preserve your privacy, especially on the internet.
wichtigste: Personal data is any information about a particular person.
In Switzerland the Data Protection Act (FADP) regulates how personal data is handled.
The revised Data Protection Act has applied since September 2023.
At federal level, the FDPIC monitors compliance with data protection.
Health data is considered especially sensitive.
In the EU the General Data Protection Regulation, GDPR for short, applies.
Cookies are small text files in the browser.
If an app asks for permission to use the microphone, it wants to access it.

abschnitte.text: **Personal data** is any information relating to a particular person, for example name, address, date of birth, photos or the location of your mobile phone. Data protection is meant to prevent such data from being collected or passed on without good reason. Everyone should be able to decide for themselves what happens to their data. This is called **informational self-determination**. In the Federal Constitution, Article 13 protects privacy and protection against misuse of personal data.

Switzerland’s first **Data Protection Act** (DSG in German) came into force in 1993. Because the digital world has changed a great deal since then, it was completely revised. The revised act has applied since 1 September 2023. It now only protects the data of natural persons, that is, of people and not of companies. For breaches, the people responsible can be fined up to 250,000 francs.

At federal level, the **FDPIC** (EDÖB in German) watches over data protection; this is the Federal Data Protection and Information Commissioner. The commissioner supervises federal authorities and private companies and can open investigations. The cantons’ own data protection officers are responsible for cantonal authorities. Every person also has a **right of access**. So you can ask what data a company has stored about you.

Some data is so sensitive that it is especially protected. This includes **health data** as well as information about religion, political views or ethnic origin. Genetic data and biometric data such as a fingerprint are also included. Anyone processing such data must be especially careful. Often explicit consent is needed for this.

Many websites store **cookies**, small text files in the browser that remember settings, for example. Apps ask for **permissions**, for example for the microphone, camera or location. If you give a permission, you allow the app to access that function. That is why you should only allow what the app really needs. Good passwords and sharing photos and data sparingly give extra protection.

Since 2018 the **General Data Protection Regulation (GDPR)** has applied in the European Union. It is one of the strictest data protection laws in the world. When it was revised, the Swiss Data Protection Act was brought closely into line with the GDPR. The EU recognises that Switzerland has equivalent data protection. That is why data can be exchanged between Switzerland and the EU fairly easily.

begriffe.erklaerung: Any information that belongs to a particular person.
The Federal Data Protection and Information Commissioner, the federal data protection authority (EDÖB in German).
A small text file that a website stores in the browser.
Allowing an app to access a function such as the camera or microphone.
The right to find out what data is stored about you.

gewusst: Since 2023 Swiss law has required privacy-friendly default settings, known in English as “privacy by default”.
Every year the FDPIC publishes an activity report about its work.

teile.einleitung: Lorry drivers take goods to where they are needed: food to the shops, building materials to the building site, parcels to the distribution centres. In Switzerland the official name of the job is road transport specialist.
wichtigste: Lorry drivers take goods from warehouses to shops and companies.
The official apprenticeship is called road transport specialist EFZ and lasts three years.
For large lorries you need a category C driving licence.
There are strict rules on driving and rest times so that nobody drives when overtired.
The work also includes loading, securing the load and checking the vehicle.
In Switzerland lorries are banned from driving at night and on Sundays.

abschnitte.text: Almost everything we buy in a shop has been in a **lorry** before. Drivers collect the goods from warehouses, factories or stations and deliver them. Some drive short distances in town every day, others are out on long journeys. There are refrigerated lorries for food, tankers for fuel and tipper lorries for gravel and soil.

There is much more to the job than steering. Drivers **load** and unload the vehicle, often with a forklift truck or a tail lift. The **load** has to be well secured so that it does not slide when braking. Before setting off, they check the tyres, lights and brakes. They plan the route and deal with the delivery papers.

The apprenticeship as a **road transport specialist EFZ** lasts three years. During the apprenticeship you take your driving licences, first for the car and then for the lorry, **category C**. For lorries with trailers you need category CE. There is also a two-year basic training course as a **road transport assistant EBA**.

A lorry is heavy and has a long braking distance. That is why **strict rules** apply. The **driving and rest times** set how long you may drive and when you have to take a break. A device in the vehicle, the **tachograph**, records this. In Switzerland lorries are in principle not allowed to drive at night from 10 pm to 5 am and on Sundays, with some exceptions.

gewusst: In Switzerland lorries pay a special charge, the LSVA (heavy vehicle charge). Part of the money goes into expanding the railways.
In Switzerland a large articulated or drawbar lorry may weigh up to 40 tonnes in total.

teile.einleitung: Farmers grow grain, vegetables and fruit and keep animals such as cows, pigs or hens. They make sure that we have milk, meat, eggs and much more to eat.
wichtigste: Farmers work on the farm, in the fields and in the cowshed.
An important vehicle is the tractor; it pulls trailers, ploughs or mowers.
Many farms in Switzerland keep cows and supply milk.
In Switzerland the apprenticeship is called farmer EFZ and lasts three years.
The work depends greatly on the weather and the seasons.
The Confederation supports farming with direct payments.

abschnitte.text: On most farms hardly anything can be done without a **tractor**. It pulls the **plough**, which loosens the soil, the seed drill and the mower. With trailers it transports hay, manure or potatoes. This makes heavy work easier that used to be done with horses or by hand. For work on slopes there are special vehicles in Switzerland that do not tip over so easily.

Many farmers keep **animals**. In Switzerland these are mainly cows for milk and meat, as well as pigs, hens, sheep and goats. The animals need food, water and a clean shed every day, even on Sundays. Cows are usually **milked** twice a day, today often with a milking machine or even a milking robot.

Wheat, maize, potatoes, sugar beet or vegetables grow in the fields. Sowing happens in spring, and the **harvest** comes in summer and autumn. To feed the animals, farmers mow the meadows and make **hay**. Because the weather is so important, they follow the weather forecasts closely. A hailstorm can destroy a whole harvest.

A large part of Switzerland consists of meadows and pastures that are well suited to cows. In summer many farmers take their animals up to the **alpine pastures**. Cheese is often made there too. The Confederation pays farmers **direct payments**, among other things for looking after the landscape and for animal-friendly farming. Many farms follow the rules of **organic farming**.

The apprenticeship as a **farmer EFZ** lasts three years. You often work on a different farm in each year of the apprenticeship, so you get to know different businesses. You learn to look after animals, grow plants and operate machines. There is also the two-year basic training as an **agricultural assistant EBA**. Anyone who runs a farm is also a business owner and has to be good with figures.

gewusst: On a warm day a dairy cow can drink more than 100 litres of water.
A modern tractor has a computer on board and, with satellite navigation, can partly drive across the field almost by itself.

teile.einleitung: Foresters look after the forest. They plan which trees are felled and where new ones are planted, and they lead the work of the forestry workers.
wichtigste: The forester works in the forest and in the office.
She decides which trees are felled.
She plans where young trees should grow.
She leads a team of forestry workers.
You become a forester through further training at a college of higher education.

abschnitte.text: A forest needs care over many decades. The **forester** checks how old and healthy the trees are. She **marks** the trees that are to be felled. This gives the remaining trees more light, and young trees can grow back. She makes sure that there are different kinds of trees in the forest.

The forester often runs a **forestry business**. She hands out the work to the **forestry workers** and to the apprentices. She sells wood, calculates costs and writes reports. That is why part of the work also takes place in the office.

The forest is there for many: for animals and plants, for the timber industry and for people who go walking or cycling. The forester advises **municipalities** and forest owners. She explains to school classes how the forest works. In the mountains she looks after the **protection forest** that guards against avalanches and rockfall.

The path usually begins with an apprenticeship as a **forestry worker EFZ**. After that comes further training as a **forester HF** at a college of higher education. People who are even more interested in science can study forestry. A love of nature and a sense of responsibility are important.

gewusst: The Swiss Forest Act protects the area of forest: if forest is cleared somewhere, a replacement usually has to be created elsewhere.
A tree that a forester plants today is often only felled many decades later.

teile.einleitung: An algorithm is a clear sequence of instructions that you use to solve a task step by step. Computers, apps and social networks work with algorithms. They decide, for example, which video is suggested to you next.
wichtigste: An algorithm is like a precise recipe with clear steps.
All computer programs are based on algorithms.
Recommendation algorithms choose content mainly based on your past behaviour.
The algorithms of many social networks are meant to keep you on the platform for as long as possible.
If algorithms mainly show content that matches your own opinion, a filter bubble is created.
By liking, searching and hiding things on purpose, you can influence the suggestions.
The word algorithm goes back to the scholar al-Khwarizmi.

abschnitte.text: An **algorithm** describes exactly what has to be done and in what order. Every step must be clear so that a result definitely comes out at the end. A cooking recipe or craft instructions work in a similar way. Written addition, which you learn at school, is also an algorithm. Computers need such precise instructions because they only do what is written in the program.

The word comes from the name of the scholar **al-Khwarizmi**, who lived in Baghdad in the 9th century. He wrote a famous book about calculating with Indian numerals. As early as around 300 BC the Greek mathematician Euclid described a method of calculation that is still used today. In the 19th century Ada Lovelace wrote an algorithm for a planned calculating machine. That is why she is considered the world’s first programmer.

Video apps, music services and online shops use **recommendation algorithms**. They watch what you look at, how long you look at it, what you like and what you skip. From this they calculate what will probably interest you next. Many platforms want you to stay as long as possible, because then you see more **advertising**. That is why it is often hard to stop scrolling.

When an algorithm mainly shows you content that matches your opinion, this is called a **filter bubble**. The term was made popular by the American Eli Pariser with a book in 2011. An **echo chamber** is a space on the internet where like-minded people strengthen each other’s opinions. Then it seems as if everyone thinks the same. That is why it is good to use other sources too, such as newspapers or news programmes.

**AI** stands for artificial intelligence. Here computer programs learn to recognise patterns from a great many examples. An AI also works with algorithms, but they are trained with huge amounts of data. In this way an AI can recognise pictures, write texts or translate languages. How it arrives at a particular result is sometimes hard to understand even for experts.

You can help shape your **feed**. If you like, search and hide unsuitable content on purpose, you change the suggestions. In many apps you can tap “Not interested” or delete your history. Some apps also offer a view without personal recommendations. Taking a deliberate break from your phone also helps you not to keep scrolling endlessly.

begriffe.erklaerung: A clear sequence of instructions for solving a task.
A situation in which algorithms mainly show you content that matches your own opinion.
A space on the internet where like-minded people strengthen each other’s views.
Short for artificial intelligence: programs that learn from data.
The list of posts that an app shows you.

gewusst: The word “algebra” also comes from the title of a book by al-Khwarizmi.
A Rubik’s Cube can always be solved with fixed sequences of moves, that is, with an algorithm.

teile.einleitung: The Data Protection Act, DSG for short in German (FADP in English), is the Swiss law that protects people’s personal data. It regulates what companies and authorities are allowed to do with your name, your photos or your health data. Since 1 September 2023 a completely renewed version has applied that fits the digital world better.
wichtigste: The Data Protection Act protects personal data in Switzerland.
The completely revised act has applied since 1 September 2023.
Only the data of natural persons, that is, of people, is protected.
The FDPIC monitors whether federal bodies and private parties comply with data protection.
Data about health or religious views is considered especially sensitive.
With the right of access you can find out what data a company has about you.
Breaches can lead to fines of up to 250,000 francs, mainly for responsible individuals.

abschnitte.titel: What is the Data Protection Act?
abschnitte.text: The **Data Protection Act** is a federal law that applies to the whole of Switzerland. It protects people’s privacy when data about them is processed. **Personal data** is any information that relates to a particular person, such as name, address, birthday, photo or mobile number. The act applies to private companies, associations and the federal authorities.

Switzerland’s first data protection act dates from 1992. At that time there were hardly any smartphones, social networks or online shops. That is why Parliament completely revised the act in 2020; this is called a **total revision**. Since 1 September 2023 the new version has applied, which is also modelled on the EU’s General Data Protection Regulation.

Some data is especially sensitive and is called **especially sensitive personal data**. This includes, for example, information about health, religious or political views, genetic data and biometric data such as fingerprints. Stricter rules apply to such data. Anyone who processes it must be especially careful.

Every person has a **right of access**: you may ask whether a company processes data about you and what data it is. Normally the company must answer within 30 days, and the information is usually free. You can also demand that incorrect data be corrected. In addition, companies must inform you when they collect data about you, for example in a privacy policy.

Companies must think about data protection right from the start when building their apps and programs; this is called **privacy by design**. With **privacy by default**, the default settings must be as privacy-friendly as possible. If data is stolen or lost, the company must report this to the FDPIC in serious cases. Anyone who deliberately breaks important duties can be fined up to 250,000 francs.

Data protection is watched over by the **Federal Data Protection and Information Commissioner**, FDPIC for short (EDÖB in German). The commissioner is based in Bern and is independent. The commissioner can open investigations into federal bodies and companies and order measures. The cantons also have their own data protection laws and data protection officers for their own authorities.

begriffe.erklaerung: Any information that belongs to a particular person, for example a name or a photo.
The independent federal office that monitors data protection (EDÖB in German).
The right to find out what data a company has about you.
Default settings must give away as little data as possible from the start.

gewusst: The new act only protects people; the old act also protected the data of companies and associations.
Unlike in the EU, fines under the Swiss act are aimed mainly at responsible individuals and not at the company.

teile.einleitung: Apprentices receive wages during their apprenticeship, often called apprentice wages. They are set in the apprenticeship contract and usually rise with each year. The wages are lower than for fully trained workers, because you are still learning.
wichtigste: Apprentice wages are set in the apprenticeship contract.
They usually rise with each year of the apprenticeship.
In Switzerland there is no legal minimum wage for apprentices.
Professional associations give wage recommendations.
The amount differs depending on the job and the region.
Social security contributions are deducted from the gross wage.
With your first wages you learn to make your own budget.

abschnitte.text: **Apprentice wages** are the money that apprentices receive from the training company every month. They are set in the **apprenticeship contract** for each year. They are lowest in the first year and usually rise after that. There is often also a 13th month's salary.

There is no legal minimum wage for apprentices in Switzerland. However, many **professional associations** publish recommendations for their industry. In the first year, depending on the job, the wages are often a few hundred francs a month. In the last year they are usually much higher.

The wage in the contract is the **gross wage**. Contributions to the AVS, disability insurance, unemployment insurance and accident insurance are deducted from it. What is left is the **net wage**, which is paid into your account. Above a certain income, apprentices also have to pay tax.

In many families, part of the wages is handed over at home, for example for food or housing. Others use it to pay for their own mobile phone contract, clothes or public transport. It is best to talk about this openly with your parents. Parents often continue to receive a **training allowance** until the end of the training.

With your first wages of your own, it is worth making a **budget**. In it you write down how much money comes in and what it is spent on. It is sensible to save a small amount every month. If you have questions, budget advice services or templates on the internet can help.

begriffe.erklaerung: Wages before any deductions.
Wages paid out after the deductions.
Old-age and survivors' insurance, the most important pension insurance in Switzerland.
A plan of how much money you take in and spend.

gewusst: In some jobs, apprentices earn more than twice as much in the fourth year as in the first.
A 13th month's salary is often paid in December and is very popular with apprentices.

teile.einleitung: An apprenticeship is a way of learning a job after compulsory school. You work in a company and go to vocational school alongside. In Switzerland many young people choose this path.
wichtigste: In an apprenticeship you learn a job directly in a company.
Alongside this you attend vocational school, usually on one or two days a week.
An apprenticeship lasts two, three or four years.
At the end there is an examination, the qualification procedure.
Apprentices receive wages.
After the apprenticeship many paths are open, including university study.

abschnitte.text: In an **apprenticeship** you learn a job by doing it. In the **training company** you work alongside others and learn step by step what is needed. At **vocational school** you add specialist knowledge and general education, such as language and society. Because practice and school alternate, this is called **dual vocational training**.

At the start, the company, the apprentice and, for those under 18, the parents sign an **apprenticeship contract**. The canton approves it. At the end of the apprenticeship comes the **qualification procedure**, the final examination. Those who pass receive a **Federal VET Diploma (EFZ)** after three or four years or a **Federal VET Certificate (EBA)** after two years.

Apprentices work and receive **apprentice wages** for it. These are lower than normal wages and rise with each year of the apprenticeship. Apprentices up to the age of 20 get at least **five weeks of holiday** a year. With their apprenticeship, many young people earn their own money for the first time and learn how to handle it.

An apprenticeship is not an end, but a beginning. With the **vocational Matura**, which you can do during or after the apprenticeship, you may study at a **university of applied sciences**. Others train further at a college of higher education or take a professional examination. That is why people in Switzerland say: **no qualification without a next step**.

gewusst: About two thirds of young people in Switzerland do an apprenticeship after compulsory school.
At the skills world championships, the WorldSkills, young skilled workers from Switzerland often win medals.

teile.einleitung: Lifelong learning means that learning does not stop when you leave school. Because jobs, technology and society are constantly changing, people keep learning all their lives, in courses, at work or simply along the way in everyday life.
wichtigste: The 1972 UNESCO report “Learning to Be”, the Faure Report, made the idea known worldwide.
The 1996 Delors Report names four pillars of education, including “learning to live together”.
A distinction is made between formal, non-formal and informal learning.
In 1885 Hermann Ebbinghaus described the forgetting curve.
Since 2006, further education has been in Article 64a of the Federal Constitution.
According to the Further Education Act, individuals themselves are mainly responsible for their further education.

abschnitte.text: In 1972 **UNESCO** published a report entitled **“Learning to Be”**. In it, a commission led by the Frenchman **Edgar Faure** called for education to last a whole lifetime. In 1996 the **Delors Report** followed. It names four pillars of education: learning to know, learning to do, **learning to live together**, and learning to be. These pillars apply to all stages of life.

Experts distinguish three forms. **Formal learning** takes place in schools and universities and leads to recognised qualifications. **Non-formal learning** happens in courses without such a qualification, for example in a language course. **Informal learning** happens just along the way, for instance when you solve a problem at work or try out a new recipe at home. A large part of our knowledge is gained in this way.

In 1885 the German psychologist **Hermann Ebbinghaus** showed with experiments that we quickly forget what we have learned. This **forgetting curve** drops steeply at the beginning. If you revise regularly, you remember more. Sebastian Leitner's **Leitner system** builds on this: flashcards move from compartment to compartment in a card box. Cards you know are revised less and less often, wrong ones start again at the front.

Today you can learn a lot on the internet. A **MOOC** is a “Massive Open Online Course”, an online course in which a very large number of people take part at the same time, often free of charge. Swiss universities such as the **EPFL** in Lausanne also offer such courses. On top of that there are learning videos, apps and learning platforms. It is still important to keep at it and apply what you have learned.

In 2006 the people accepted new articles on education. Since then, further education has been in **Article 64a** of the Federal Constitution. The **Further Education Act** is based on it. It states that **individuals** themselves are first and foremost responsible for their further education. Employers should support them, and the state helps in addition. If you pay for work-related further education yourself, you can deduct it from your taxes; for direct federal tax for 2025 up to a maximum of 13,000 francs.

gewusst: According to Ebbinghaus, you forget a large part of what you learned within the first few hours unless you revise.
Older people also often keep learning, for example at universities for senior citizens.

teile.einleitung: A crane lifts heavy loads up high and moves them through the air. On building sites it is essential, and it is controlled by a crane operator.
wichtigste: With a crane you lift heavy loads such as concrete slabs, steel girders or pallets of bricks.
Crane operators control the crane, often from a cab high up.
Today many cranes are also operated with a remote control from the ground.
On building sites you often see the tower crane, on the road the mobile crane.
A counterweight stops the crane from tipping over.
In Switzerland you need a crane operator's licence for many cranes.

abschnitte.text: A **crane** is a machine for lifting and moving heavy loads. A **hook** hangs from a steel cable. The loads are attached to it. The crane can raise and lower the hook, move it along the jib and turn round. This way it takes material exactly to where it is needed, for example to the fifth floor of a new building.

On building sites there is often a **tower crane**: a tall tower with a long horizontal arm, the **jib**. A **mobile crane** sits on a lorry and drives from job to job. In factory halls, **overhead cranes** run along the ceiling. In ports, large cranes lift containers off ships. Every crane is built for a particular job.

abschnitte.titel: Why it does not fall over
abschnitte.text: A crane works like a giant pair of **scales**. On one side hangs the load, on the other side there are heavy concrete blocks as a **counterweight**. This keeps the crane balanced. The further out a load hangs, the lighter it has to be. That is why every crane has a table showing how much it may lift at which point.

The **crane operator** sits in the cab or controls the crane with a **remote control**. She needs good eyesight, calm and a lot of concentration. She communicates with people on the ground by radio or with hand signals. In Switzerland you do training for this work and receive a **crane operator's licence**. In strong winds no work is done, for safety reasons.

gewusst: The ancient Romans already built cranes with a treadwheel, in which people walked to pull the load up.
The crane bird gave the crane its name, because the long jib reminds people of its neck.

teile.einleitung: Computer scientists work with computers and programs. They write software, set up devices and networks and help when something does not work.
wichtigste: Computer scientists work mainly with computers and programs.
They write programs in programming languages.
They set up computers, servers and networks.
The apprenticeship as an IT specialist EFZ lasts four years.
Today computer science is needed in almost every industry.

abschnitte.text: A **program** is an exact set of instructions for the computer. Computer scientists write such instructions in a **programming language**. This is how apps, websites or programs for companies are created. Before a program is finished, it is thoroughly **tested** so that no errors remain.

Other computer scientists look after the **devices**. They set up computers and servers and connect them into a **network**. They make sure that data is backed up and protected from attacks. When something is not working, they look for the fault and fix it.

The apprenticeship as an **IT specialist EFZ** (Informatikerin or Informatiker EFZ) lasts four years. You choose a specialism, for example **application development** for programs or **platform development** for devices and networks. Another apprenticeship is **ICT specialist EFZ**. After the apprenticeship you can go on to study at a university of applied sciences.

**Logical thinking** and enjoying puzzles are important. If you can solve problems step by step, you have a good starting point. Computer scientists often work in a team and explain to customers how something works. Since technology changes quickly, you keep learning throughout your working life.

gewusst: In 1950 ETH Zurich started using Konrad Zuse's Z4, one of the first working computers in Europe.
The Swiss computer scientist Niklaus Wirth developed the programming language Pascal at the ETH.

teile.einleitung: A magnifying glass makes small things look big. Watchmakers, goldsmiths and many other skilled workers need one for their fine work.
wichtigste: A magnifying glass makes small things visible in a larger size.
It consists of a curved lens, known as a converging lens.
Watchmakers need a magnifying glass because the parts in a watch are tiny.
You clamp the watchmaker's loupe directly into your eye, so both hands stay free.
You must never look at the sun through a magnifying glass.

abschnitte.text: A **magnifying glass** consists of a **lens** that is thicker in the middle than at the edge. It is called a **converging lens**. As light passes through the glass it is refracted, which means bent. If you hold the magnifying glass close to an object, it looks bigger to the eye. Typical magnifying glasses magnify about two to ten times. For even smaller things you need a **microscope**.

In a mechanical watch there are tiny **wheels**, springs and screws, some hardly bigger than a grain of sand. So that the **watchmaker** can see them, she uses a **watchmaker's loupe**. She clamps this small magnifier directly into her eye. This leaves both hands free for tweezers and screwdriver. In Switzerland the apprenticeship as a **watchmaker EFZ** lasts four years.

It is not only watchmakers who work with magnifying glasses. **Goldsmiths** check precious stones, **electronics technicians** inspect fine soldered joints, and stamp collectors examine their stamps closely. A magnifying glass is also worthwhile in nature: with it you can discover insects, leaves or stones. A bright workplace helps, because with good light you can see more.

gewusst: Switzerland is famous worldwide for its watches; many watch companies are in the Jura Arc, for example in the Vallée de Joux.
A magnifying glass can focus sunlight so strongly that paper starts to burn. That is why it is also called a burning glass.

teile.einleitung: A college of higher education, HF for short, is a school for skilled workers who want to get ahead after their apprenticeship. You do not need a Matura for it, but usually a completed apprenticeship. The HF is part of higher vocational education and leads to a federally recognised diploma.
wichtigste: HF is the abbreviation for college of higher education.
You can attend one after an apprenticeship without a Matura.
The HF is part of higher vocational education.
At the end you receive a federally recognised HF diploma.
Many people attend the HF while working.
Well-known examples are nursing HF or engineering HF.

abschnitte.text: Colleges of higher education are schools at **tertiary level**, which means after an apprenticeship or secondary school. They prepare skilled workers for specialist and management roles. The teaching is very practical. Together with the federal examinations, the HF make up **higher vocational education**.

There are HF in many fields, for example engineering, business, health, social work, hospitality and art. Well known, for instance, is the qualified nurse **HF**. Technicians HF in mechanical engineering or computer science are also in demand. If you go to a hotel management school, you are also doing an HF.

A full-time course at an HF usually lasts two to three years. But many people attend the school **alongside their job** and keep working. Then the training usually takes three to four years. Internships or a diploma project are often part of it.

At the end there is a **diploma** recognised by the Confederation, for example qualified technician HF. With it you can take on more demanding tasks and often earn more. In some cases you can then go on to study at a university of applied sciences. This makes the HF an important building block in Switzerland's flexible **education system**.

The costs of an HF vary depending on the school and the canton. Many cantons support students by paying contributions to the schools. Employers often also pay part of the costs. Careers advice helps you to find the right HF.

begriffe.erklaerung: The level of education after an apprenticeship or the Matura.
Further training for skilled workers who have completed an apprenticeship.
Learning while continuing to work in your job at the same time.
Official confirmation that you have passed a course of training.

gewusst: Colleges of higher education in this form exist almost only in Switzerland.
Many nurses in Swiss hospitals did their training at a college of higher education.

teile.einleitung: The paint roller is one of the most important tools in the painting trade. With it you can paint large surfaces such as walls and ceilings quickly and evenly.
wichtigste: A paint roller is made up of a handle, a frame and a roller that turns.
The roller has a cover that soaks up the paint.
With a roller you can paint large surfaces much faster than with a brush.
For corners and edges you still need a brush.
Painters learn how to use the roller during their apprenticeship.

abschnitte.text: The paint roller has a **handle** and a bent **frame**. The **roller** turns on the frame. A cover made of synthetic fibre, foam or fleece sits over the roller. The cover soaks up the paint and releases it again as it rolls.

First you dip the roller into the paint. Then you wipe it on a **paint grid** so that not too much paint is left on it. After that you roll it over the wall in even strips. This gives a smooth surface without drips or streaks.

There are wide rollers for walls and narrow ones for small surfaces. Smooth doors need a different cover from rough plaster. With a **telescopic pole** you can even reach high ceilings without climbing a ladder.

In Switzerland you learn the trade of **painter EFZ** in a three-year apprenticeship. Painters paint walls, building fronts, doors and windows. They prepare the surface, cover the floors and mix colours. Besides the roller they use brushes, filling knives and spray guns.

gewusst: After work you have to wash the roller out well, otherwise the cover goes hard.
A good roller leaves hardly any splashes if you move it slowly and evenly.

teile.einleitung: A deepfake is a picture, video or sound recording that has been faked with artificial intelligence and looks deceptively real. This makes it possible to have people seem to say or do things they never said or did. Deepfakes can be funny, but they can also be misused for fraud and lies.
wichtigste: A deepfake is a fake picture, video or sound created or changed with AI.
The term comes from a Reddit username from 2017.
Many deepfakes are made with Generative Adversarial Networks, GANs for short.
Fraudsters use cloned voices to pretend to be bosses or relatives.
The EU’s AI Act requires deepfakes to be labelled.
Because of deepfakes, people can also deny that real recordings are genuine.

abschnitte.text: The word is made up of **deep learning** and the English word fake. Deep learning is a method of artificial intelligence in which computers learn from a great many examples. The term became known in 2017 through a Reddit user who called himself deepfakes. Today it is used for all deceptively real AI fakes of faces, bodies and voices.

Often a **Generative Adversarial Network** works with two programs competing against each other. The generator creates fakes, and the discriminator tries to spot them. Both keep getting better, like two chess players who constantly practise against each other. Today other AI methods are also used, and just a few seconds of a voice recording can be enough to imitate a voice.

Using cloned voices, fraudsters phone people and pretend to be a boss or a family member. They claim it is an emergency and urgently demand money. Deepfakes are also used to put false statements into the mouths of politicians. Fake nude pictures, which humiliate and hurt people, are especially bad.

Not every deception needs AI: in a **cheapfake** or shallowfake, a video is simply slowed down, cut or wrongly captioned. Another problem is the **liar’s dividend**. Because everyone knows that deepfakes exist, people can simply claim that real embarrassing recordings are fakes. This makes it harder to trust evidence.

Signs of a deepfake can be strange blinking, blurred edges around the face, wrong lighting or lips that do not match the sound. The **C2PA** standard, also called Content Credentials, is meant to make it possible to trace where pictures and videos come from and how they have been edited. The EU’s AI Act requires deepfakes to be labelled as artificially created or altered. With suspicious calls, it helps to hang up and call the person back yourself on the number you know.

In Switzerland every person has a right to their own image and voice, which is part of **personality protection**. Anyone who spreads a hurtful deepfake of someone without permission can therefore face legal action. Depending on the case, criminal law may also apply, for example for fraud, defamation or blackmail. The police advise reporting attempts at fraud with fake voices.

begriffe.erklaerung: An AI method in which a computer learns from huge numbers of examples.
Two programs, one of which fakes and the other tries to expose the fake.
A deception made with simple means such as cutting or slowing down.
Real recordings are denied as supposed fakes.

gewusst: The idea of GANs was presented by the researcher Ian Goodfellow in 2014.
In March 2022 a fake video appeared in which the Ukrainian president Zelensky supposedly called for surrender.

teile.einleitung: Cyberbullying is when someone is repeatedly humiliated, insulted or excluded via mobile phone, the internet or social networks. Because your phone is always with you, it can go on around the clock. Those affected need help, and bystanders can also make a big difference.
wichtigste: Cyberbullying is repeatedly humiliating someone via digital media.
It is often especially distressing because it can go on around the clock.
Those affected save evidence with screenshots.
With the Block function you stop a person from writing to you any more.
Pro Juventute helps children and young people on the number 147.
Bystanders who do not step in often make the bullying worse.
In Switzerland cyberbullying can be a criminal offence, for example as insult or threat.

abschnitte.text: In **cyberbullying**, someone is deliberately and repeatedly put down via digital media. This happens, for example, with nasty messages, embarrassing photos, lies or fake profiles. Deliberately excluding someone from a class chat can also be part of it. Often the bullies and the victim know each other from school. But sometimes the bullies act anonymously.

Unlike bullying in the playground, cyberbullying does not stop after school. It can go on **around the clock**, right into your own room. A picture or video can spread to a great many people in a short time. Once something is on the internet, it is very hard to delete it again. Those affected often feel helpless, sad or ashamed.

The most important thing is to talk to a **trusted person**, for example your parents or a teacher. With **screenshots** you save evidence before messages are deleted. You should not reply to nasty messages. With the **Block** function you stop a person from writing to you any more, and you can report them to the platform. Pro Juventute offers help around the clock on the number 147, also by chat.

Many people see cyberbullying but do not step in. They are called **bystanders**. Anyone who forwards nasty posts, likes them or laughs about them makes the bullying worse. On the other hand, anyone who supports the person affected, gets help or reports posts can change a lot. Often only a few brave people are needed for the bullying to stop.

In Switzerland there is (as of 2026) no separate criminal offence of cyberbullying. But many acts are still criminal offences, for example as **insult**, defamation, threats or coercion. Spreading intimate pictures without consent is also forbidden. In Switzerland, young people aged 10 and over can be punished under **juvenile criminal law**. For some years Parliament has been discussing a separate criminal law against cyberbullying.

begriffe.erklaerung: Repeatedly humiliating, insulting or excluding someone via digital media.
A picture of the screen that you can use to save evidence.
People who watch bullying but do not step in.
A feature that stops a person from writing to you any more.
Criminal law for young people aged 10 to 18, which aims above all to educate.

gewusst: The German word “Mobbing” comes from the English “to mob”, which means to crowd round someone and attack them.
A call to Pro Juventute’s number 147 is free and confidential.

teile.einleitung: Hairdressers cut, wash, colour and style hair. In Germany people say Friseur, while in Switzerland the word Coiffeur is usual. The job combines craft, creativity and working with people.
wichtigste: Hairdressers cut and colour hair.
In Switzerland the job is called Coiffeuse or Coiffeur.
The apprenticeship with EFZ lasts three years.
There is also a two-year apprenticeship with EBA.
Advising customers is an important part of the work.
You spend a lot of time standing and working with your hands.

abschnitte.text: Hairdressers **advise** their customers and suggest hairstyles that suit them. They wash, cut, colour and style the hair. Some also create updos for weddings or look after beards. They use scissors, combs, hairdryers and hair clippers.

The apprenticeship as a hairdresser **EFZ** lasts three years. People who prefer learning in a practical way can do the two-year apprenticeship with **EBA**. You work in the salon and attend vocational school. In inter-company courses you often practise techniques on training heads.

When **colouring** hair and doing perms, hairdressers work with chemical products. They need to know how these affect hair and skin. That is why they also learn something about skin, hair and chemistry at school. Protective gloves protect their own hands from irritation.

A love of fashion and of contact with people is important. You need skilful hands and a good eye for shapes and colours. Since you stand almost all day, good health is important. Patience and friendliness are also part of the job, because the **customers** should feel comfortable.

After the apprenticeship you can specialise, for example in colours or wedding hairstyles. With a **professional examination** or an advanced professional examination you can train further. Many experienced hairdressers later open their own salon. Some also work in the theatre, film or television.

begriffe.erklaerung: A shop where hair is cut and cared for.
The Swiss word for hairdresser; it comes from French.
A treatment that makes straight hair stay curly for a long time.
A product used to change the colour of the hair.

gewusst: The word Coiffeur comes from the French word coiffer, which means to do someone's hair.
In the past, barbers did not only cut hair but also pulled teeth.

teile.einleitung: The tall white chef's hat is the best-known sign of the cooking profession. It looks good, but above all it has a practical job: it protects the food from hairs.
wichtigste: Cooks often wear a tall white chef's hat.
The hat keeps the hair together so that no hairs fall into the food.
In French the chef's hat is called a “toque”.
White shows straight away whether the clothing is clean.
Today many cooks also wear smaller hats, caps or hairnets.

abschnitte.text: In a kitchen, **hygiene** is very important. A hair in the food is unpleasant for guests and can carry germs. The **chef's hat** covers the head and keeps the hair together. It also soaks up some sweat, because it gets hot at the cooker. Because it is **white**, you can see stains straight away and know when it needs to go in the wash.

The tall, pleated hat is called a **toque** in French. It became well known in French cooking and today is a symbol of cooks all over the world. A well-known **legend** says that the many pleats stand for the many ways in which a good cook can prepare eggs. Whether this is true is not certain, but people like telling the story.

In everyday work many cooks no longer wear a tall toque, but a low **hat**, a **cap**, a headscarf or a **hairnet**. All that matters is that the hair is covered. Chef's clothing also includes the **chef's jacket** made of thick fabric, which protects against splashes, an apron and non-slip shoes.

gewusst: The chef's jacket often has two rows of buttons, so if it gets a stain you can button it the other way and it looks clean again.
The chef's hat is so well known that it is often used as a symbol for restaurants or cookbooks.

teile.einleitung: Gardeners work outdoors with plants. They lay out gardens, plant flowers and trees, trim hedges and mow the lawn.
wichtigste: Gardeners plant and look after flowers, trees, shrubs and lawns.
They usually work outdoors and in almost all weathers.
Some design and build gardens, others raise plants in a nursery.
The apprenticeship as a gardener EFZ lasts three years.
There is also a two-year training course with a vocational certificate.

abschnitte.text: In **landscape gardening**, gardeners lay out new gardens. They build paths, walls, steps and ponds. They plant trees, shrubs and flowers. Afterwards they **look after** the grounds: they trim **hedges**, mow the **lawn** and remove weeds. Parks and school playgrounds are also cared for in this way.

Other gardeners work in **plant production**. They sow seeds, grow cuttings and look after the young plants in the **greenhouse** or in the field. These include flowers, perennials, vegetable seedlings or young trees in a **tree nursery**. Later the plants are sold.

Gardeners need many tools: a **spade**, rake, shears, watering can and wheelbarrow. For big jobs they use machines, for example lawnmowers, hedge trimmers or small diggers. They also know which plant needs which soil and how much light.

The apprenticeship as a **gardener EFZ** lasts three years. You choose a specialism, for example landscape gardening or plant production. If you would like a shorter training course, you can do the two-year apprenticeship with a vocational certificate (**EBA**). A love of nature and of physical work is important.

gewusst: Gardeners have to know many plant names, often the Latin names too.
After the apprenticeship you can train further, for example up to the master craftsman's examination or at a university of applied sciences.

teile.einleitung: Confectioners are experts in sweet things. In the patisserie they make gateaux, cakes, pastries and chocolates that are often almost too beautiful to eat.
wichtigste: The confectioner makes gateaux, cakes, desserts and chocolates.
People who make chocolates and chocolate are also called chocolatiers (Confiseur or Confiseurin).
In Switzerland the apprenticeship is called baker, pastry chef and confectioner EFZ and lasts three years.
Exact weighing is important, because with dough and cream every gram counts.
Confectioners need skill and a sense for colours and shapes.
The work often starts very early in the morning.

abschnitte.titel: What is made in the patisserie
abschnitte.text: In a **patisserie**, sweet treats are made: gateaux with cream and fruit, cream slices, cakes, biscuits and desserts. For birthdays or weddings, confectioners make **celebration cakes** to order. This also includes **decorating** with glaze, chocolate, marzipan or icing. There is often a small café next to the shop as well.

Making chocolates, truffles and chocolate figures is called **confectionery**. For this, chocolate has to be properly **tempered**: it is warmed and cooled exactly so that it later shines and snaps. Switzerland is famous all over the world for its chocolate. Many confectioners make their chocolates by hand.

In Switzerland you learn the job in the apprenticeship as a **baker, pastry chef and confectioner EFZ** (Bäcker-Konditor-Confiseur EFZ). It lasts three years. You choose a specialism, for example patisserie and confectionery. There is also a two-year basic training course with **EBA**. At vocational school you learn, among other things, how to calculate recipes and about hygiene.

In baking, **precision** is important. Too much flour or too little sugar, and the dough does not turn out well. That is why confectioners weigh everything exactly and pay attention to temperature and time. At the same time they are **creative**: they design gateaux in many shapes and colours. Because the goods should be fresh, the work often starts early in the morning.

gewusst: Zug cherry cake (Zuger Kirschtorte) is a well-known Swiss cake that is soaked with kirsch.
The German word Konditor comes from the Latin “condire”, which means to season or to preserve.

teile.einleitung: Florists work with flowers and plants. They tie bouquets, create flower decorations for celebrations and advise their customers in the flower shop.
wichtigste: Florists usually work in a flower shop.
They tie bouquets and make arrangements and wreaths.
They decorate rooms for weddings, celebrations and funerals.
They look after the flowers so that they stay fresh for a long time.
The apprenticeship as a florist EFZ lasts three years.
